cards.name: TNT cobblestone wall farm (autocraft walls, shulker-load, bulk sell)
cards.source: web/p1.txt | ggwtb blog 'Donut SMP Money Guide: Best Cobblestone Farm Meta After the Update' | author SMITH | posted 06/23/26
cards.setup_time: Not stated in hours. Phased: build 1 TNT test module and run it 10 minutes, then scale to 6–9 modules, then to a full 16-module bunker.
cards.capital_required: Not stated in money ('cheap to build'). Needs TNT dupers, water+lava generators, hoppers or water streams, crafters, shulker loaders, a supply of empty shulker boxes, buffer storage, hidden base, safe AFK platform, sell setup.
cards.claimed_gross_per_hour: Clean setup 40M–60M per hour. Starter (1–2 modules) 5M–15M/hour; mid-size farm 25M–45M/hour; large 16-module bunker 45M–60M+/hour; full-day AFK 'hundreds of millions to 1B+' only if storage and uptime are clean.
cards.claimed_profit_per_hour: Same as gross (no per-unit input cost is stated; TNT is duped, cobble is generated).

outputs.channel: sell (implied: article says 'sell in bulk' and lists 'sell tools or sell access' as first reinvestment; exact channel not named)

cards.process: 1. Water + lava generate cobblestone. 2. TNT dupers break it. 3. Drops move through hoppers or water streams. 4. Crafters turn cobble into walls. 5. Walls load into shulker boxes (shulker loader). 6. Full shulkers eject and move into storage. 7. Sell in bulk. Build order: Phase 1 one test module (confirm TNT breaks cobble, add collection, add crafting, add shulker loading, run 10 minutes to find jams). Phase 2 scale to 6–9 modules with checklist (enough empty shulkers, no item buildup, crafters never jam, full shulkers eject cleanly, output chests have space, TNT dupers stay synced, safe AFK spot). Phase 3 16-module bunker with buffer storage, multiple shulker loaders, hidden entrance, repair kit, safe AFK platform, sell setup. AFK-friendly: 'Makes money while you are not actively grinding'.
quotes: A clean setup can hit 40M–60M per hour.
Starter 1–2 modules 5M–15M | Mid-size farm 25M–45M | Large 16-module bunker 45M–60M+ | Full-day AFK Hundreds of millions to 1B+
Do not trust one lucky minute of output. Test for 10 minutes, count the shulkers, then multiply by six.
If your farm is not crafting or loading fast enough, more TNT modules will not fix it. They will just create overflow.
Once the test module works, expand to 6–9 modules. This is the sweet spot for most players.
tricks: Timed test: run 10 minutes, count shulkers, multiply by six for an honest hourly number.
Build stable, then scale: one test module first; 'If one module breaks, sixteen modules will break louder.'
Item transport by hoppers or water streams (also 'water or ice path'); walls go through a shulker loader; full shulkers must eject into storage automatically.
Before 16 modules add buffer storage, multiple shulker loaders, hidden entrance, repair kit, safe AFK platform, sell setup.
Check water before every serious test: 'One missing water source can turn your money machine into a crater.'
Overflow: stop the farm immediately, then check crafters, shulker loader, empty shulker supply, output chests, water or ice path, hopper lines.

Loader diagnostics: empty shulkers present? output chest full? full shulkers ejecting? loader receiving items too fast? redstone failed to reset? 'If the loader only breaks during AFK, your input speed is too high or your storage is too small.'
Chests fill unevenly = bad distribution, rework hopper/water routing. TNT blows up farm = missing water or bad TNT path.
Raid defense: move deeper, hide access, split storage; hidden underground base first (progression stage 1).
Reinvest first profits into: shulker boxes, storage chests, redstone repair materials, TNT module supplies, PvP gear for defense, hidden base materials, extra loaders, 'sell tools or sell access'.
cards.risks: Overflow (lost money, lag, makes farm noticeable), TNT destroying the farm when water is missing, shulker loader failing during AFK, chests filling unevenly, server lag, raids ('Farm gets raided: poor location security'). Profit depends on module count, server lag, TNT timing, crafter speed, loader reliability, chest space, sell access, raid safety, AFK uptime.
cards.scalability: Limited by crafter speed and shulker-loader throughput, empty shulker supply, chest space, server lag, and 'sell access'. Article says adding modules beyond what loaders/crafters handle only creates overflow. Sell-axe cost and its 24h self-destruct timer would bound bulk-sell throughput if the sell axe is the channel (not stated in article).
cards.still_valid_after_june_2026_update: yes (article is post-update, 06/23/26, and calls cobble walls 'now one of the best ways to print money'). Caveat: sell channel and per-wall price never stated; with the sell multiplier removed, the /worth base price of cobblestone walls decides the real number.

cards.name: Bookshelf autocrafter flip (books + logs -> bookshelves into /orders)
cards.source: web/p2.txt | ggwtb blog 'Donut SMP Money Guide: Best Auto Crafter Flips, Bookshelf Profit, and Pumpkin Farm Strategy' | author SMITH | posted 05/09/26 (pre-update)
cards.capital_required: 1.4M for one batch (books 1.2M + logs 200k) producing ~650 bookshelves.
cards.claimed_gross_per_hour: Not hourly. Per batch: sale revenue 2.05M at 3.15k each (~650 bookshelves). Scaling table: 4k each -> 2.6M; 4.6k -> 2.99M; 8k -> 5.2M.
cards.claimed_profit_per_hour: Per batch: ~650k profit (~46% return) at 3.15k; 1.2M at 4k; 1.59M at 4.6k; 3.8M at 8k (all after 1.4M cost).

inputs.item: Leather, paper, logs (stock before spikes if crafting books yourself)

outputs.unit_price: 3.15k each (example); watch at 4k+; craft fast at 8k
outputs.channel: orders (first, if prices are high); ah only if demand is slow but prices better

cards.process: Check /orders for expensive items, check material prices in AH/player market, compute cost per craft, compare to sell price, craft a small batch, scale only if it sells fast. Craft books yourself when possible (buying finished bookshelves kills margin). Use a multi-item auto crafter that stops when one input runs out. Sell into /orders first if prices are high; use AH only if demand is slow but prices are better. Stop crafting the moment material cost rises too high.
quotes: Books cost 1.2M | Logs cost 200k | Total material cost 1.4M | Bookshelves crafted ~650 | Sale revenue 2.05M | Profit ~650k
That is around a 46% return from one batch.
If bookshelves hit 4k+, we start watching hard. If they hit 8k, we craft fast and sell before the market floods.
If bookshelves sell for 4k+ and your crafting cost is around 2.2k, the margin is strong.
tricks: Stock leather, paper, and logs before prices spike.
Use an auto crafter that stops when one input runs out; otherwise 'it can craft the wrong item and jam the system. Build safety into the design.'
Sell into /orders first if prices are high; AH only if demand is slow but prices are better.
Margin rule: good margin 25%+ after costs, great margin 40%+ especially if items sell instantly; skip tiny margins.
Sell when prices spike; 'Waiting for a little more often ends with everyone dumping the same item.'
Reliability over speed: 'A fast crafter that clogs is worse than a slower one that runs clean.'
cards.risks: Price crashes fast after order spikes; ingredient costs can rise ('A bookshelf selling for 4k is not profit if materials cost 3.9k'); holding too long.
cards.scalability: Limited by /orders volume for bookshelves and by material supply (books/leather/paper); AH fallback is slot-limited (18 default).
cards.still_valid_after_june_2026_update: unknown. Pre-update source (05/09/26). The mechanics (orders + autocrafter) still exist; prices of books/logs/bookshelves and order volume must be rechecked. No /sell or multiplier dependency, so the method is structurally intact.

cards.process: Auto crafters convert spruce logs -> planks -> chests (8 planks per chest; 1 spruce log = 4 planks; 2 logs per chest). Buy logs when cheap and store; craft and sell into chest orders when chest price > 2 x log price; stop immediately when below.
quotes: Farm size 14 x 16 x 23 | Logs used ~600K spruce logs | Log price ~85 each | Input cost ~54M | Chest sell return ~28M | Net result ~26M loss | Main issue Chest price too low
Minimum profitable chest price = 2 x log price
Log Price 60 -> Cost Per Chest 120 -> Chest Sell Price Needed Above 120 | 70 -> 140 | 80 -> 160 | 85 -> 170 | 100 -> 200
If logs cost 85, your material cost per chest is 170. If chests sell for 125, you lose 45 per chest before storage or market delays.
tricks: Rule: chest price > 2 x log price -> craft and sell; chest price < 2 x log price -> stop immediately.
Logs are cheap -> buy and store; chest orders are high -> sell fast; everyone is crafting chests -> wait; cannot sell instantly -> do not overproduce.
'Chest crafters are closer to market flipping than farming.'
cards.risks: High market risk; input cost above output value; unsold stock.
cards.scalability: Chest order volume; log supply price.

mechanics_facts.fact: Cobble wall farm loop: water+lava generate cobblestone, TNT dupers break it, drops move through hoppers or water streams, crafters make walls, walls load into shulkers, full shulkers move to storage, sell in bulk.
Honest hourly test: run 10 minutes, count shulkers, multiply by six.
Adding TNT modules beyond crafter/loader capacity only creates overflow; overflow is lost money, causes lag and makes the farm easier to notice.

Shulker loader failure checklist: empty shulkers present, output chest not full, full shulkers ejecting, input speed not too high, redstone reset; if it only breaks during AFK, input speed too high or storage too small.
Reinvestment list includes 'Sell tools or sell access' (implies sell axe / sell tool as the bulk-sell channel for farm output).
Profit formula: Profit = sell price minus material cost; good margin 25%+ after costs, great margin 40%+ if items sell instantly.
Auto crafter safety: if one ingredient runs out and the crafter keeps firing it can craft the wrong item and jam; use a crafter that stops when one input runs out.
Flying machines can desync or stop on multiplayer servers; design pumpkin factories with access to every layer.

Pre-update selling choice: /orders when order price > normal sell value; /sell when your sell multiplier beats orders; AH when players overpay; event selling when the server boosts crop prices. (Sell multiplier was removed 2026-06-02/03.)
Crafted items are often better through /orders when demand spikes; crop items were better through /sell when the multiplier was high.
A chest needs 8 planks; one spruce log gives 4 planks; one chest needs 2 logs; minimum profitable chest price = 2 x log price.
Bonemeal farm: a signal dispenser controls linked modules; one bad dispenser can kill output across the whole line. Fuel ~80K bonemeal per 20 modules.
Build money farms at deep slate level, low-traffic region, hidden entrance; use shulker storage plus an overflow hopper line to stop item despawn; keep the chunk loaded.

Update changes: /shop removed (harder to buy mobs and key resources), sell multiplier removed (old AFK farms make less), orders matter more, skeleton access nerfed (bones and bone meal more important), prices move faster.
Auction House is usually more expensive than orders; buy gold, bones, bone meal, iron, chests and bulk farm materials through orders; use AH only when speed matters more than margin.
Test-small rule: buy $100K–$500K of input, run one batch, sell output, check profit, scale only if the math works.
Profit = Output value minus Input cost minus Build cost; a farm costing $1M making $50K/hour needs 20 hours to break even.
One bone meal on birch-forest grass yields around 4–6 wildflowers; wildflowers only spawn in birch forest biome.
Chest minecarts are in demand because players use them in traps.
Ender pearl farm rates tank if endermen can spawn outside the platform; clear nearby spawning areas.
New metas crash quickly: supply rises, order prices drop, margins shrink, late builders get stuck.
AH vs orders rule: AH = more money, slower sale; orders = faster, usually cheaper; if players need it for PvP, farms, bases or enchanting, AH usually wins; craft then sell gives best margins.
List potions in small batches to avoid AH slot waste; sell anvils individually because they move faster; sell leather in bundles of 10/32/45.
Order-filling trick: place a buy order slightly above current buyers to get filled, then resell on AH.
Silk Touch needed for packed ice, coral (dies otherwise), emerald ore, nether gold ore.
Snow golem needs 2 snow blocks + carved pumpkin; shovel the snow layer under a trapped golem for infinite snow.
Sheep farm module: observer detects grass change, dispenser with shears, hopper minecart collects, chest stores.
Cured librarian can sell Mending books for 1 emerald.
Trial chambers: do not buy expensive keys unless you already found unopened vaults.
Shard shop consumables row removed: ender pearls, golden carrots, totems, ender chests, oak wood, arrows. Weapons, tools and armor stayed with same enchants and prices.
AFK shard farming removed (because of mass alt farms); Shard Booster removed; standing still for over an hour did not trigger an AFK kick in testing.
Homes menu shows first 5 homes by default (Show More for the rest); old team homes moved into personal home slots; no homes deleted.
Home teleport is instant with no cooldown; RTP is instant with a 14–15 second cooldown and is blocked while moving or falling. Use /home to escape before entering the void.
Auction purchase history removed; Quick Buy Confirmation is a toggle in settings (new General tab) alongside Night Vision and Mob Spawning toggles.
Amethyst pickaxe (shard tool) duration cut from 3 days to 24 hours at the same shard cost, same performance.
Billford daily trade route removed.
Piglin trading buffed on paper (shop no longer sells pearls, obsidian, crying obsidian) but live testing showed piglins may trade slowly on the server.
Border expansion expected to shake the market (travel gear, storage, food, PvP supplies, base materials).
